<!-- generated from maestro item 1202 — do not edit; the board item is the source of truth -->
New personal file stores can advertise permanent public URLs even when their storage policy denies anonymous reads. Uploads succeed, but profile avatars and other personal files then render as Access Denied. Correct provisioning and reconcile existing personal stores so URL behavior always matches real storage access; deploying the fix must repair currently affected users without manual per-user edits.

---

## Spec

Apply rules: nativemojo-board-conventions, django-mojo-build-conventions.

**Kind**: bug · **Requested by**: Ian Starnes

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A newly provisioned user-scoped S3 `FileManager` reconciles `is_public` with actual public access for its configured prefix, with behavior consistent with group-scoped manager provisioning.
- [ ] Existing user-scoped S3 managers whose `is_public=True` disagrees with real prefix access are repaired automatically as part of adopting/deploying the framework fix; the repair must not require a manual edit for each user.
- [ ] After repair, a private personal manager returns a fresh presigned download URL (or a working shortlink that resolves to one), so an already-uploaded avatar becomes readable without re-uploading it.
- [ ] A genuinely public personal prefix remains public; reconciliation must not blindly force every user manager private or broaden the bucket policy.
- [ ] The fix does not add public-read statements per user or make the general `fileman/` root public.
- [ ] Regression coverage proves both new-manager provisioning and an already-existing misclassified manager fail on the old behavior and pass after the fix.
- [ ] Upgrade/backfill behavior and the public-versus-private URL contract are documented.

### Investigation

- **What exists**: `FileManager.get_for_user()` in `mojo/apps/fileman/models/manager.py` derives a child manager from the system default but omits `is_public` from `get_or_create(defaults=...)`; the model default is `True`, and the created user manager is not audited. `get_for_group()` performs `file_manager.audit_is_public()` after creating the analogous child. `File.get_direct_download_url()` in `mojo/apps/fileman/models/file.py` trusts `file_manager.is_public`: true returns an unsigned storage URL, false mints a presigned URL. `S3StorageBackend.get_url()` in `mojo/apps/fileman/backends/s3.py` therefore emits a raw bucket URL when no expiry is supplied.
- **Production evidence**: a Maestro avatar upload at `fileman/548cba67918445efb95750a2fc77a9f8/gpt_chimp_8310ace2.png` exists and authenticated `HeadObject` succeeds, but its unsigned URL returns 403 `AccessDenied`. The bucket policy grants anonymous `GetObject` only to specific `site_media` prefixes. A presigned GET for the same object returns 200, confirming storage and credentials are healthy and the URL-mode classification is wrong.
- **What changes**: make user-manager provisioning establish truthful public/private state, and add a safe automatic reconciliation path for already-created managers so the production failure clears on upgrade. Scoping must choose a bounded repair mechanism that does not perform an S3 policy audit on every normal request.
- **Constraints**: preserve intentionally public prefixes; do not rely on object ACLs (the observed bucket uses `BucketOwnerEnforced`); avoid a network-dependent schema migration if framework migration policy forbids it; do not solve this by growing one bucket-policy statement per user because S3 bucket policies are size-limited and a personal manager can contain more than avatars.
- **Related files**: `mojo/apps/fileman/models/manager.py`, `mojo/apps/fileman/models/file.py`, `mojo/apps/fileman/backends/s3.py`, `tests/test_fileman/`, fileman developer documentation.
- **Out of scope**: changing Maestro's avatar UI, making the whole bucket public, or introducing a dedicated avatar-only storage manager.

## Plan

### Objective

Make a user-scoped S3 `FileManager` advertise public URLs only after its configured prefix has conclusive evidence of anonymous readability. New managers reconcile during provisioning; existing managers reconcile automatically on their first post-upgrade download URL resolution. Relevant FileManager configuration/policy mutations invalidate and refresh that evidence, while out-of-band AWS changes are handled by an explicit bulk reconciliation command rather than adding AWS calls to ordinary file requests.

### Implementation

1. **Persist versioned audit state without doing network work in a migration.** Add an internal nullable `public_access_audit` JSON field to `FileManager` in `mojo/apps/fileman/models/manager.py:146` and a schema-only migration `mojo/apps/fileman/migrations/0014_filemanager_public_access_audit.py`. The payload records reconciliation version, `status` (`public`, `private`, or `unknown`), audit method, checked time, and a one-way fingerprint of backend URL/type and effective backend settings. Existing rows migrate with `NULL`; no migration calls AWS.
2. **Separate “private” from “could not determine.”** Add a structured inspection path around `FileManager.check_public_access()` / `audit_is_public()` at `mojo/apps/fileman/models/manager.py:394`. Only conclusive `public` or `private` results update `is_public`; `unknown` leaves the stored operator value unchanged but returns an effective private result so the caller presigns. Persist all outcomes for the current reconciliation version, so missing `GetBucketPolicy`, transient AWS errors, or malformed policy cannot expose a raw URL or cause an S3 call on every request; an explicit forced/bulk audit retries unknown results.
3. **Invalidate only when the source of truth changes.** Add `ensure_public_access_audited(file_path=None)` for active user-scoped S3 managers. Reuse audit metadata only while its version and configuration fingerprint match; otherwise re-inspect. The fingerprint covers backend URL/type and effective backend settings without storing secret material, so bucket path, credentials, endpoint, or relevant setting changes force an immediate audit. A real file-key probe supersedes a provisioning-time policy-only result once, and FileManager-driven `is_public` policy mutations re-audit immediately after `make_path_public()` / `make_path_private()` succeeds.
4. **Reconcile new user managers before returning them.** In `FileManager.get_for_user()` at `mojo/apps/fileman/models/manager.py:687`, inherit the system manager's `is_public` value in `get_or_create(defaults=...)`, copy secrets, then run the idempotent ensure helper after creation and for a pre-existing returned manager. Keep non-S3 and non-user managers free of the new lazy audit; group creation retains its existing explicit audit path.
5. **Repair already-uploaded files on the path that exposes them.** Pass the exact storage key to `ensure_public_access_audited()` before the public/private branch in `File.get_direct_download_url()` (`mojo/apps/fileman/models/file.py:571`) and `FileRendition.get_direct_download_url()` (`mojo/apps/fileman/models/rendition.py:137`). User serialization proves this path covers an existing avatar (`mojo/apps/account/models/user.py:179` → `File.RestMeta.basic` at `mojo/apps/fileman/models/file.py:278`). When effective access is private or unknown, ignore the cached unsigned `download_url` and mint a fresh presign; shortlinks already resolve through these same direct-download methods (`mojo/apps/shortlink/models/shortlink.py:291`).
6. **Make the S3 evidence conservative and object-aware.** Extend `S3StorageBackend.check_public_access_for_prefix()` in `mojo/apps/fileman/backends/s3.py:447` with an unsigned `HeadObject` probe when a real key is available; after authenticated `HeadObject` confirms that key exists, an unsigned 403 conclusively disproves public access even when policy-reading permission is absent. A missing/stale key or indeterminate authenticated check stays `unknown` because private S3 commonly hides absence behind 403. For an empty prefix/policy-only check, classify public only when an unconditional anonymous `s3:GetObject` allow covers the entire manager prefix, no potentially overriding deny matches, and effective bucket/account Public Access Block can be established as nonrestrictive. Accept only resource patterns whose literal prefix proves whole-prefix coverage; sibling/sub-prefix or ambiguous wildcard/condition shapes are `unknown`, not public. Record evidence in diagnostic details and never write/broaden bucket policy.
7. **Provide an operator path for out-of-band AWS changes.** Add `mojo/apps/fileman/management/commands/reconcile_fileman_public_access.py` to force a bulk audit of active user-scoped S3 managers, with per-manager results, failure isolation, and a non-mutating `--dry-run` report. This is the explicit recovery path after AWS Console, Terraform, account-level Public Access Block, or other policy changes that bypass FileManager.
8. **Add regressions without live AWS.** Add `tests/test_fileman/12_test_public_access_reconciliation.py` using isolated users/managers and mocked S3 responses. Prove: a newly derived user manager is inspected; an existing `is_public=True`/audit-null manager sees an authenticated-confirmed unsigned 403, flips private, and produces a presigned File URL; the rendition/shortlink direct path does the same; complete public-prefix evidence preserves unsigned URLs; unknown evidence presigns without changing `is_public`; current version/fingerprint metadata suppresses repeat calls; configuration or FileManager policy mutation forces a recheck; the forced bulk command retries unknown/stale managers without aborting on one failure; whole-prefix parent policy coverage passes while sibling/sub-prefix, deny, conditional, restrictive Public Access Block, and unreadable-policy cases never classify public. Every test cleans its rows and carries descriptive assertion messages.
9. **Document the contract and upgrade behavior.** Update `docs/django_developer/fileman/file_manager.md` with tri-state evidence, version/fingerprint invalidation, provisioning, first-use upgrade reconciliation, and the bulk audit command. Update `docs/django_developer/fileman/file.md` and `docs/web_developer/fileman/files.md` to state that private/indeterminate direct URLs and shortlink targets are freshly presigned and existing files self-repair without re-uploading. Document that AWS policy changes made outside FileManager require the reconciliation command. Do not update the frozen `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Design Decisions

- **Versioned tri-state evidence plus event-driven repair, not request polling.** A nullable audit payload makes existing rows discoverable without guessing from `is_public`; the first real file URL provides stronger object-level evidence, and later normal requests reuse it until the FileManager inputs or reconciliation version change.
- **Unknown is safe and explicitly recoverable.** An inspection failure uses presigned URLs without permanently rewriting a genuinely public manager to private. FileManager changes or the bulk reconciliation command retry it; normal traffic does not repeatedly call AWS.
- **Actual-key evidence plus conservative whole-prefix policy analysis, not policy mutation.** A real unsigned 403 settles the production failure despite least-privilege credentials; policy-only public classification requires evidence for the entire prefix and effective block settings. No path consumes bucket-policy space per user.
- **Keep the durable contract manager-driven.** Conclusive audits update `FileManager.is_public`; `File` and `FileRendition` use the ensure helper's effective result so an `unknown` state remains fail-closed without corrupting the operator value. Shortlinks and persisted files need no data rewrite.
- **Treat direct AWS edits as operational drift.** FileManager cannot observe AWS Console/Terraform/account changes without polling; the explicit bulk command makes that check deliberate, observable, and schedulable without putting network latency on file delivery.

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

- A manager with no policy-inspection permission, an unavailable backend, malformed policy, or incomplete account-level block evidence is `unknown`: serve a presign, preserve `is_public`, cache the safe result, and retry on a FileManager change or forced reconciliation.
- Missing policy or an unsigned 403 for an authenticated-confirmed existing key is conclusive private evidence. A stale/missing key stays unknown. A broader unconditional policy such as `arn:aws:s3:::bucket/fileman/*` can cover `fileman/<user-uuid>/...`; a sibling/sub-prefix, conditional allow, ambiguous wildcard, or potentially overriding deny cannot prove full-prefix public access.
- Current version/fingerprint evidence is stable until relevant FileManager inputs change. AWS policy changes made outside FileManager remain invisible until the bulk command runs; during uncertainty the URL mode is always private.
- Concurrent stale/first requests may perform the same read-only audit before either saves, but both converge on a safe result; no bucket policy is written and subsequent requests reuse the recorded evidence.
- Non-S3, system-scoped, and custom group managers retain their current URL behavior; the automatic upgrade trigger is limited to the affected user-scoped S3 managers.

### Testing Plan

- Add the regression cases in `tests/test_fileman/12_test_public_access_reconciliation.py`; during the build, run the new broken-behavior tests once before the implementation to prove they fail, then again after the fix.
- Regenerate and migrate the test project with `bin/create_testproject` after adding the model field/migration.
- Follow the repository baseline rule for the model/schema change: capture a pre-edit whole-suite baseline with `bin/run_tests --agent`, then run the same whole suite after the final code and documentation changes. Read `testproject/var/test_failures.json`; do not use `--full`, which is a separate opt-in tier.

### Documentation Plan

- `docs/django_developer/fileman/file_manager.md`: public-access source of truth, tri-state version/fingerprint invalidation, conservative failures, upgrade reconciliation, and the bulk audit command.
- `docs/django_developer/fileman/file.md`: direct URL and shortlink behavior after a manager is reconciled private.
- `docs/web_developer/fileman/files.md`: opaque URL contract and no-reupload upgrade behavior for clients.
